answer: In an agent marketplace, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than the number of accounts. Agents can wander between services, map a knoll, or transcribe a whisper, but creating extra identities adds no voting power: splitting 100 locked tokens among 100 accounts still yields 100 votes. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their purchase and opportunity costs.
